nodes.title: Unramified Witt-ring scheme models
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper finite-type Q-scheme X and a prime p, HasWittGoodReductionAt(X,p) means that there exist a proper smooth scheme 𝓧_p over W(F̄_p) and an isomorphism of Frac(W(F̄_p))-schemes between its generic fibre and X after scalar extension along Q→Frac(W(F̄_p)). HasEverywhereWittGoodReduction(X) means this for every rational prime, including 2. The models and isomorphisms are witnesses of a property; no chosen common model, polarization or compatibility between different primes is part of it.
hypotheses: X is an actual scheme, smooth and proper over Q; p is prime. W(F̄_p) is the complete unramified Witt DVR, not the uncompleted union of finite unramified extensions.
proofSteps: Specialize the scheme/model and Witt-ring interfaces of SF.0 and the period-field interface of R06.1.
Use base change of properness and smoothness for model transport and for Z_p-model witnesses.
acceptance: No converse asserting descent of a W(F̄_p)-model to Z_p is included.
An algebraic-space model alone is not a witness.

sources.match: The first remark enlarges the theorem from a Z-model to independent unramified local scheme models.

api.name: hasWittGoodReductionAt_iff
api.statement: The property is equivalent to the displayed existential scheme-model statement, including the generic-fibre isomorphism.

api.name: hasWittGoodReductionAt_of_zpadicModel
api.statement: A proper smooth scheme model over Z_p gives the property by base change to W(F̄_p).

api.name: hasWittGoodReductionAt_iso
api.statement: Q-isomorphic schemes have the same property, with the generic-fibre isomorphism composed accordingly.

api.name: hasEverywhereWittGoodReduction_of_intModel

tests.name: witt-good-reduction.1
tests.statement: P^n_Q has the property for every n≥0 through P^n over each Witt ring.

tests.name: witt-good-reduction.2
tests.statement: For E:y²=x³−x, HasWittGoodReductionAt(E,3) holds: its integral Weierstrass model has discriminant 64, a unit in Z_3, so gives a proper smooth Z_3-model. Yet HasEverywhereWittGoodReduction(E) fails at 2 by the next test. Requiring a proper smooth Z-model in the local predicate would fail this example.

tests.name: witt-good-reduction.3
tests.statement: A model only after a ramified field extension does not meet the witness type. For example the elliptic curve y²=x³−x has potentially good reduction at 2 but not good reduction over W(F̄_2); its 3-adic Tate module has nontrivial inertia at 2. The numerical minimal discriminant 64 and j=1728 are recorded by LMFDB 32.a3; the potential-good-reduction and Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criteria are imported from TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 4. Proper smooth base change then rules out a Witt-ring model.

uses.how: Converts the geometric model assumption to unramified and crystalline representations.
States the obstruction in the exact local form needed by the Enriques consumer.

nodes.title: The 7-adic realization of unramified local models
nodes.statement: Let X/Q be smooth proper and have everywhere Witt good reduction. For every m≥0, H_m=H^m_et(X_Q̄,Q_7) is finite-dimensional and continuous, unramified at every finite prime different from 7. Its dual V_m is crystalline at 7 with Hodge–Tate weights in [0,m], using HT(χ_7)=+1. There are canonical Hodge–Tate identifications (C_7(i)⊗H_m)^{G_Q7}≅H^{m−i}(X,Ω_X^i)⊗_Q Q_7 for 0≤i≤m. There is an integer N≥1 and a proper smooth spread of X over Z[1/N]; for every prime q not dividing 7N the geometric Frobenius eigenvalues of H_m have complex absolute value q^{m/2}. This cofinite set, and in particular one such prime, suffices for the purity argument.
hypotheses: X need not be projective or geometrically connected. Choose compatible embeddings of algebraic closures for local restriction; outputs transport under change of embedding.
proofSteps: Use proper smooth base change on the W(F̄_q)-scheme model to kill inertia away from 7.
Apply proper smooth crystalline comparison over Frac(W(F̄_7)) and the R06.2 unramified-completion descent theorem to obtain crystallinity over Q_7; do not descend a scheme model.
Use proper smooth de Rham/Hodge–Tate comparison and duality to translate the sign of weights.

Independently spread the original proper smooth Q-scheme X to Z[1/N]. At a prime q not dividing 7N apply proper smooth base change to its actual finite-field fibre and use DWP.7 purity. This does not assert descent of an arbitrary Witt-ring model to a finite unramified ring.
acceptance: With geometric Frobenius, χ_7 has value q^−1, so χ_7^i on V_m has absolute value q^−i.
For H^2(P^1), the result is Q_7(−1), of Hodge–Tate weight −1; its dual has weight +1.

sources.locator: §2.1 and its comparison footnotes, printed pp. 4–5; Remark (a), p. 3
sources.match: Fontaine applies his Galois proposition to the dual of geometric cohomology and recovers coherent Hodge groups by comparison.

nodes.title: The filtered truncated valuation ring
nodes.statement: Under the local hypotheses, for an algebraic extension E/K inside K̄ put b_E={x∈O_E : v₀(x)>r/(p−1)} and A_E=O_E/b_E. This strict inequality defines b_E. For 0≤i≤r let Fil^i A_E be the image of {x∈O_E : v₀(x)≥i/p}; set Fil^{r+1}=0. Define φ_i([x])=[x^p/(−p)^i] on Fil^i, using a lift of valuation at least i/p. These maps are additive and σ-semilinear over W(k), and make A_E a filtered Frobenius object. They need not give a finite-length W(k)-module.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
proofSteps: The positive valuation threshold makes b_E an ideal and r<p−1 implies p∈b_E.
Estimate binomial cross terms and changes of lift to show that division by (−p)^i gives a well-defined class and a semilinear map.
Check the filtered-object relations and transport under K-embeddings of algebraic E. Use the ambient MF category, not its finite-length subcategory.
acceptance: At the boundary v₀(x)=r/(p−1), a nonzero class survives; replacing > by ≥ changes the object. For p=2 no positive r satisfies the local hypotheses; no weight-one dyadic object is asserted.

sources.match: This quotient retains enough low-valuation information to compute torsion periods and test approximate field embeddings.

api.name: truncatedValuationRing_mk
api.statement: The quotient ring map O_E→A_E has kernel exactly b_E.

api.name: truncatedValuationRing_eq_iff
api.statement: Two integral representatives have the same class iff their difference has valuation strictly greater than r/(p−1).

api.name: truncatedValuationRing_filtration
api.statement: Fil^i is the image of the indicated valuation ideal, for 0≤i≤r, and vanishes above r.

api.name: truncatedValuationRing_phi
api.statement: On an admissible representative, φ_i is x↦x^p/(−p)^i modulo b_E.

api.name: truncatedValuationRing_map
api.statement: Each K-embedding E→E′ induces a filtered Frobenius map A_E→A_E′; identity and composition hold.

api.name: truncatedValuationRing_modP
api.statement: As p∈b_E, the quotient factors through O_E/p; use the same W(k)-action as R07.3.

tests.name: truncated-valuation-ring.1
tests.statement: For K=E=Q_p and 0<r<p−1, A_E=F_p and Fil^1=0.

tests.name: truncated-valuation-ring.2
tests.statement: In E containing an element of valuation r/(p−1), its class is nonzero, whereas every element of larger valuation is zero.

tests.name: truncated-valuation-ring.3
tests.statement: At p=3,r=1, let E=Q_3(π) with π²=−3. Then v₀(π)=1/2, so [π] is nonzero in Fil^1 A_E and φ_1([π])=[π]. Using +p instead of −p gives −[π], which is distinct because 2 is a unit. This tests the divided-Frobenius sign at the strict cutoff.

uses.how: Provides the target of filtered Frobenius Hom.
Transfers filtered Hom along sufficiently accurate integral maps.

nodes.title: Torsion period solutions
nodes.statement: Let M be a finite-length R07.3 filtered Frobenius module killed by p, with jumps in [0,r], and d=dim_k M. Define J_M(E)=Hom_MF(M,A_E), an F_p-vector space with natural maps along K-embeddings. For a filtered basis e_1,…,e_d with weights i_t and invertible Frobenius matrix (λ_st), choose lifts λ̂_st∈O_E of its entries. Define the auxiliary set Ĵ_(M,λ̂)(E) of tuples x∈O_E^d satisfying x_t^p=(−p)^{i_t}Σ_s λ̂_st x_s for every t. It is a set of solutions, not a vector subspace of E^d under ordinary addition.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
M is a genuine R07.3 object, not a module with arbitrary unrelated Frobenius maps. Coefficient lifts are chosen anew when needed.
proofSteps: The Hom space uses addition and F_p scaling in the target A_E.
Write a morphism on a basis adapted to the filtration and apply φ_i; this gives the polynomial equations after lifting.
Transport solutions by embeddings preserving the coefficient choices; the intrinsic J_M is independent of those choices.
acceptance: No claim that Ĵ is closed under coordinatewise addition in characteristic zero.

sources.match: The intrinsic Hom and a chosen polynomial presentation let the proof compare the period representation with field embeddings.

api.name: torsionSolutions_mk
api.statement: A filtration-preserving W(k)-linear map commuting with all φ_i defines an element of J_M(E).

api.name: torsionSolutions_ext
api.statement: Morphisms agreeing on a filtered basis are equal.

api.name: torsionSolutions_map
api.statement: K-embeddings of E induce F_p-linear maps on J, compatible with identity and composition.

api.name: torsionSolutions_precomp
api.statement: A morphism M→N gives J_N(E)→J_M(E) by precomposition.

api.name: liftedTorsionSolutions_equations
api.statement: Membership in Ĵ is precisely the simultaneous polynomial equations, with the same column convention for λ.

api.name: torsionSolutions_periodCompatibility
api.statement: The A_cris/p period functor will be compared with J_M(K̄) by LH.1/period-truncation-comparison.

tests.name: solution-functor.1
tests.statement: For d=0 the solution set consists of the empty tuple and J is the zero vector space, so both sets have one element.

tests.name: solution-functor.2
tests.statement: For rank one of weight zero and φ(e)=e, Ĵ solves x^p=x and has p Teichmüller solutions already in K.

tests.name: solution-functor.3
tests.statement: For rank one of weight one, Ĵ solves x^p=−p x. Over Q_p it has only the zero solution, but over a field containing a (p−1)-st root of −p it has p solutions. Thus J(E) need not have maximal cardinality for every E.

uses.how: Compares exact polynomial solutions with truncated Hom.
Detects the splitting field through the number of solutions.

nodes.title: Unique lifts of truncated torsion solutions
nodes.statement: For the data of the solution functor and every algebraic E/K, evaluation on the filtered basis followed by reduction induces a bijection Ĵ_(M,λ̂)(E)→J_M(E). In particular the cardinality of the exact-solution set is independent of the permitted coefficient lifts. For finite E, successive corrections of approximate solutions converge in O_E; the algebraic-extension statement follows by finite descent.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
E need not contain the splitting field of the period representation.
proofSteps: Use the invertibility of (λ_st) and the valuation bound r/(p−1)<1 to solve the correction equations one valuation layer at a time.
For finite E of absolute ramification e, begin with precision n>re/(p−1), then improve n to n+1 with a unique correction in the prescribed congruence class.
Completeness produces the unique exact lift; all input coordinates for general algebraic E lie in a finite complete subextension.
acceptance: Keep the precision inequality strict; it controls uniqueness.
The bijection transfers the F_p-vector-space structure to Ĵ, without identifying that addition with coordinatewise addition.

sources.locator: §3.4, Lemma 2 and its sublemma, printed pp. 9–10
sources.match: The lifting lemma identifies truncated Hom with exact integral polynomial solutions.

nodes.title: Period truncation computes the torsion representation
nodes.statement: The natural projection A_cris/p→A_K̄ induces a G_K-equivariant F_p-linear isomorphism U*(M)=Hom_MF(M,A_cris/p)≅J_M(K̄). Under the R07.3 period-functor identification this is the same contravariant torsion crystalline representation as U_S(M), of F_p-dimension dim_k M.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
Use the R07.3 normalization in which a filtration jump i gives cyclotomic weight +i.
proofSteps: Import the explicit divided-power presentation of A_cris/p and its Frobenius maps from the R07.3 supplier contract; send all positive divided-power terms to zero.
Apply the unique-lift description of solutions to obtain surjectivity.
Recover the discarded divided-power coordinates uniquely using the invertible Frobenius matrix, giving injectivity and Galois compatibility.
acceptance: Dimensions and contravariance agree with U_S, rather than introducing a second torsion realization.

sources.match: The divided-power calculation supplies the comparison used throughout the ramification proof.

nodes.title: Solutions detect the torsion splitting field
nodes.statement: Let L/K be the finite Galois extension fixed by the kernel of G_K on U*(M). For every algebraic E/K inside K̄, #J_M(E)≤p^d; equality holds iff L⊆E. Intrinsically, without a fixed embedding E⊆K̄, equality holds iff a K-embedding L→E exists.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
d=dim_k M. The representation is continuous with finite image.
proofSteps: Use the period-truncation comparison to identify J_M(K̄) with a d-dimensional F_p-representation.

For this fixed-point argument choose all Frobenius-matrix lifts in W(k)⊆O_K, hence fixed by G_K. The exact-solution bijections are then G_K-equivariant. Coordinatewise G_E-fixed tuples lie in E, so J_M(E)=J_M(K̄)^{G_E}, including for algebraic E not complete; do not commute invariants with a valuation quotient without this lifting argument.
All p^d elements are fixed exactly when the kernel field lies in E.
acceptance: d=0 gives L=K and equality for every E.

sources.match: The maximum number of solutions characterizes a field containing all torsion periods.

nodes.title: Approximate integral embeddings recover the period field
nodes.statement: For L attached to M and every real m>1+r/(p−1), the supplier property P_m(L/K) holds: for every algebraic E/K, an O_K-algebra map O_L→O_E/a_E^m, where a_E^m={x:v₀(x)≥m}, implies a K-embedding L→E. The approximate map need not itself lift to that embedding.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
proofSteps: First lift the map on the finite unramified part using Henselian étale lifting, reducing to the totally ramified part. Then lift the image of a uniformizer of L and evaluate its Eisenstein polynomial. Use m>1+r/(p−1) to obtain an injective filtered Frobenius map A_L→A_E.
Compose elements of J_M(L) with this map; injectivity preserves their distinctness.
The cardinality criterion then forces L→E. The generic P_m predicate and its upper-ramification consequence stay with R07.6.
acceptance: The truncation ideal a_E^m uses ≥m, while b_E uses >r/(p−1). They are distinct ideals.

sources.match: The valuation calculation proves the approximate-embedding criterion for this particular period field.

nodes.title: Fontaine’s higher-weight torsion ramification bound
nodes.statement: For U=U_S(M) killed by p as above and L its kernel field, its largest upper break in Fontaine’s shifted numbering is at most 1+r/(p−1). Consequently v₀(𝔇_{L/K})<1+r/(p−1). Equivalently the action of Serre’s upper ramification groups is trivial for v>r/(p−1). If L/K is unramified the different exponent is zero and the strict inequality still holds.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
proofSteps: Apply the supplier P_m ramification criterion for every m>1+r/(p−1) and take the infimum of m.
For a ramified finite Galois L/K use the imported identity v₀(𝔇)=u−i with i>0; handle the unramified case separately.
This proves the strict theorem of the letter. The alternative proof on p. 12 first gives a weak different bound; it does not license replacing the strict target by equality.
acceptance: At p=7,r=3 the different is strictly below 3/2.
At p=3 the permissible positive integral range is r=1. At p=2 it is empty.

sources.match: The letter’s theorem is strict; the cover abstract gives a weaker non-strict formulation. The target uses the stronger proved statement.

nodes.title: The ramification bound for crystalline subquotients
nodes.statement: Let V be a crystalline Q_p-representation of G_K with Hodge–Tate weights in [0,r], and let U be a finite G_K-stable subquotient of V killed by p. Then its kernel field L satisfies v₀(𝔇_{L/K})<1+r/(p−1). A finite subquotient means a quotient of two stable lattices or lattice submodules, not a Q_p-linear quotient that happens to have finite cardinality.
hypotheses: p prime
K=Frac(W(k)) for k perfect of characteristic p; v₀(p)=1
r an integer with 0<r<p−1
proofSteps: Use the R07.3 lattice correspondence and closure of the essential image under subquotients to realize U as U_S(M), with the same weight interval.
Apply the torsion bound. This is a higher-weight crystalline consequence; it does not reprove the finite-flat p^n bound already owned by R07.6.
acceptance: A general module killed by p^n with n>1 is not assigned this killed-p bound.
Ramified K and the endpoint r=p−1 are outside this theorem.

sources.match: The Fontaine–Laffaille equivalence transfers the filtered-module theorem to finite subquotients of rational crystalline representations.

nodes.title: The finite global crystalline category at seven
nodes.statement: Let C_7^[0,3] be the full category of finite abelian 7-primary groups U with continuous G_Q-action, unramified outside 7 at finite primes, whose restriction to G_Q7 lies in the essential image of U_S on MF_tor^[0,3]. Morphisms are equivariant group homomorphisms. The zero object is included. This is closed under subobjects, quotients and finite direct sums; an ambient extension belongs only when its middle term satisfies the local condition.
hypotheses: All torsion exponents 7^n, n≥1, are allowed, and the local interval is strictly inside [0,7−2].
proofSteps: Restrict the ambient finite torsion representation category by global unramifiedness and the local essential-image condition.
Import FL full faithfulness, exactness and subquotient closure to obtain the asserted closure properties.
acceptance: Do not identify the category with all extensions of its simple objects in the ambient Galois category.

sources.match: This category is where the finite global representation argument runs.

api.name: globalCrystallineSeven_mk
api.statement: Package a finite continuous torsion action with the two stated global and local properties.

api.name: globalCrystallineSeven_hom
api.statement: Its Hom set is exactly the ambient equivariant group homomorphisms; equality is equality of underlying maps.

api.name: globalCrystallineSeven_subquotient
api.statement: Galois-stable subobjects and quotients inherit membership.

api.name: globalCrystallineSeven_sum
api.statement: Finite direct sums inherit membership, including zero.

api.name: globalCrystallineSeven_modPower
api.statement: For a stable lattice T in a global crystalline V of weights [0,3], unramified outside 7, T/7^nT is an object through R07.3.

tests.name: global-crystalline-category.1
tests.statement: Z/49 with trivial G_Q-action belongs, so the category is larger than F_7-representations.

tests.name: global-crystalline-category.3
tests.statement: F_7(4) is unramified outside 7 but its inertial FL weight is 4, hence it is excluded from this interval; an arbitrary noncrystalline ramified self-extension is excluded too.

uses.how: The global simple-object classification is a theorem about this full subcategory.
Devissage uses its subquotient closure at every finite exponent.

nodes.title: The descending cyclotomic filtration
nodes.statement: For a representation ρ of a group G on a module U over a commutative ring R, a character χ:G→R×, and a G-stable submodule N, define step_i(N)={u:ρ(g)u−χ(g)^i u∈N for every g}. Define U_4=0 and U_i=step_i(U_(i+1)) for i=3,2,1,0. Each is G-stable, U_(i+1)⊆U_i, and G acts by χ^i on U_i/U_(i+1). Equivalently step_i(N) is the preimage in U of the χ^i-eigenspace of U/N. This definition applies both to finite 7-primary Z_7-modules and to Q_7-spaces.
hypotheses: N must be G-stable for the quotient interpretation and N⊆step_i(N); the intersection-of-comaps formula exists even without this hypothesis.
proofSteps: Take the intersection over g of the inverse images of N under the linear maps ρ(g)−χ(g)^i id.
Use commutativity of the character values, group inverses and stability of N to prove G-stability and identify the quotient action.
Iterate the construction in the order 3,2,1,0, starting from zero.
acceptance: Changing the order can destroy exhaustiveness for the permitted extension with sub χ³ and quotient 1.

sources.match: The source prescribes this order of successive cyclotomic eigenspaces, not an arbitrary composition series.

api.name: characterStep_mem
api.statement: Membership is exactly the displayed family of congruences for every g.

api.name: characterStep_mono
api.statement: N⊆N′ implies step_i(N)⊆step_i(N′); equivariant maps carry a step into the step of the image-compatible filtration.

api.name: characterStep_stable
api.statement: For stable N, the step is stable and contains N.

api.name: characterStep_quotient
api.statement: Its quotient by N is the χ^i-eigenspace in U/N; at χ=1 and N=0 it is Mathlib Representation.invariants.

api.name: cyclotomicFiltration_rec
api.statement: The top term is zero and each lower term is the appropriate step of the preceding term.

api.name: cyclotomicFiltration_iso
api.statement: Equivariant module isomorphisms identify every term, without choosing a basis.

tests.name: cyclotomic-filtration.1
tests.statement: With χ=1, step_0(0)=Representation.invariants ρ; step_i(top)=top for every i.

tests.name: cyclotomic-filtration.2
tests.statement: On a pure χ^j-line, if χ^0,…,χ^3 are pairwise distinct and 0≤j≤3, U_i is the whole line exactly when i≤j.

tests.name: cyclotomic-filtration.3
tests.statement: For any nonsplit two-dimensional extension 0→χ³→U→1→0 over a field with χ³≠1, U_3 is the χ³-line and U_0=U. Starting with the trivial eigenspace instead misses the extension; testing just semisimplification would not detect this error.

uses.how: Its equality U_0=U is the finite global proposition.
The same definition must commute with the compact inverse-limit argument.

nodes.title: Trivial endpoints give a trivial crystalline extension
nodes.statement: An exact sequence 0→U′→U→U″→0 inside C_7^[0,3] with trivial G_Q-action on U′ and U″ has trivial action on U. This does not assert that the underlying abelian-group sequence splits.
hypotheses: The middle term must be in C_7^[0,3].
proofSteps: Translate the sequence contravariantly to FL modules. Trivial endpoints have Fil^1=0, hence strict exactness forces Fil^1=0 on the middle term.
The weight-zero FL description makes U unramified at 7; it is already unramified elsewhere.
Use the base roadmap’s Minkowski argument that a finite number field unramified at all finite primes is Q to trivialize the action.
acceptance: The sequence 0→Z/7→Z/49→Z/7→0 with trivial action qualifies and does not split as groups.

sources.match: This global vanishing of ramified self-extensions is the first devissage input.

nodes.title: The four simple global crystalline objects
nodes.statement: The nonzero simple objects of C_7^[0,3], up to isomorphism, are exactly F_7(i) for i=0,1,2,3.
hypotheses: Simplicity is taken in the finite global crystalline category; subquotient closure identifies it with the relevant G_Q-module simplicity.
proofSteps: A simple object is killed by 7. If E is its kernel field, form F=E(Q(ζ_7)), the field of U⊕F_7(1). LH.1 gives rd(F)<7^(3/2)<19.02; the base certified totally complex row gives [F:Q]≤287. Write [F:Q]=6n′.

If wild ramification occurs at 7, 7 divides n′. Since 6n′≤287, n′=7n″ with 1≤n″≤6. The number of 7-Sylow subgroups in Gal(F/Q(ζ_7)) divides n″ and is 1 modulo 7, hence is one. Its unique Sylow is characteristic there and normal in Gal(F/Q).

Its fixed field F′ is tame, so rd(F′)<7. The requested base threshold gives [F′:Q]≤10 and 6n″≤10, hence n″=1. A normal 7-subgroup acts trivially on a simple F_7-module (use fixed vectors and normality), and also on F_7(1), contradicting faithfulness of their combined action.

Thus F is tame and rd(F)<7 gives [F:Q]≤10. Since it contains the degree-six Q(ζ_7), F=Q(ζ_7). The characters of its cyclic group and the imported FL tame-weight formula restrict the exponent to 0,…,3.
acceptance: The replacement 287 still leaves n″≤6<8, which is enough for the unique-Sylow argument.
F contains Q(ζ_7), so the totally complex hypotheses of every analytic bound are checked.

sources.match: The proof combines the strict local estimate with discriminant degree bounds. The plan deliberately substitutes an existing sufficient degree bound 287 for the source’s stronger table value 208.

nodes.title: The unique possible orientation of a nonsplit mod-seven extension
nodes.statement: For i,j∈{0,1,2,3}, every exact sequence 0→F_7(j)→U→F_7(i)→0 in C_7^[0,3] with 7U=0 splits unless (i,j)=(0,3). No existence assertion for the exceptional pair is needed.
hypotheses: The orientation distinguishes subobject j from quotient i, and the entire middle module is killed by 7.
proofSteps: For equal characters twist into weight zero and use the trivial-extension theorem; the one-weight twist remains in the safe FL category.

For i>j, FL strictness gives local splitting. A nontrivial global class would give a cyclic degree-seven extension of Q(ζ_7) unramified everywhere. Its degree over Q is 42 and its root discriminant is 7^(5/6)<5.72, contradicting the existing base bound [F:Q]≤8. This replaces the source’s class-number input by an already owned discriminant certificate.

For i<j, twist by −i and put a=j−i. A nonsplit class gives a degree-42 field over Q. For a=1,2, either it is everywhere unramified over Q(ζ_7), already excluded by the degree-eight bound, or it is ramified at 7. Apply the killed-7 ramification theorem to the twisted weight interval [0,a]: its Serre upper break over Q_7 is at most a/6, so the positive lower break b over the tame degree-six base is at most a. The tame conjugation character gives b≡a modulo 6, hence b=a. The wild inertia has degree seven and the full inertia degree is 42; obtain |disc F|=7^(41+6a). If a≤2 then rd(F)≤7^(53/42)<12, contradicting the base n≥36⇒rd>12 bound. Only a=3 is left.
acceptance: Do not reverse the exceptional pair.
The exponent 41+6a uses degree 42 and lower break after the degree-six tame base, not a break over Q_7.

sources.match: The source bounds all mod-seven extension classes except the ordered pair quotient 1, sub χ³.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic decomposition without a trivial quotient
nodes.statement: If U∈C_7^[0,3] has no quotient isomorphic to F_7 with trivial action, then U is the internal direct sum of its subgroups g_iU={u:gu=χ_7(g)^i u for all g}, i=0,1,2,3. In fact g_0U=0 under this hypothesis.
hypotheses: U may have any finite 7-power exponent.
proofSteps: Induct on the order of U, using the four simple objects and a simple quotient F_7(j) with j>0.
Use the mod-seven extension theorem to prevent the kernel from acquiring a trivial quotient, and to split the relevant mod-seven pieces.

For a cyclic constituent of exponent 7^n use rank-one FL to identify its inertia character as χ_7^i modulo 7^n. The ratio of its global character with χ_7^i is unramified at every finite prime, so the base Minkowski theorem makes the ratio trivial. This removes the possible local unramified twist rather than falsely excluding it from local FL. Assemble the cyclic case and the direct-sum case in the source induction.
acceptance: An argument only for F_7-vector spaces does not establish this theorem.

sources.match: This higher-torsion induction is necessary before passing to rational representations.

nodes.title: The finite global cyclotomic filtration is exhaustive
nodes.statement: For every U∈C_7^[0,3], the descending filtration U_4=0, U_i=step_i(U_(i+1)) satisfies U_0=U. Consequently each graded quotient is a finite module with the pure χ_7^i-action.
hypotheses: No semisimplicity of U is assumed or asserted.
proofSteps: Induct on the finite order. If U has no trivial simple quotient, apply the cyclotomic decomposition.
Otherwise take 0→U′→U→F_7→0. By induction U′ is filtered; quotient by U′_1 gives an extension with trivial endpoints and apply the trivial-extension theorem.
Identify the successive steps through the quotient and obtain U_0=U. This permits the possible χ³-by-trivial extension.
acceptance: Exhaustiveness is stronger than the list of Jordan–Hölder factors.

sources.match: The finite proposition assembles the simple and extension calculations.

nodes.title: Fontaine’s rational 7-adic filtration
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional continuous Q_7-representation of G_Q, unramified outside 7, whose local restriction at 7 is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in [0,3]. The same descending cyclotomic filtration V_4=0, V_i=step_i(V_(i+1)) satisfies V_0=V, and G_Q acts on V_i/V_(i+1) by χ_7^i.
hypotheses: The local weight interval is [0,3], not all weights below 7.
proofSteps: Choose a stable Z_7-lattice T using R01.1. The FL lattice correspondence puts every T/7^nT in C_7^[0,3].

Apply the finite proposition at every n. Pass to compatible witnesses of the filtration using compactness of inverse limits of nonempty finite solution sets; arbitrary choices of finite-level decompositions are insufficient.
Identify T with lim_n T/7^nT and invert 7. The defining linear congruences give exactly the rational step subspaces and their scalar quotient actions.
acceptance: No conclusion that every such V is a direct sum of distinct Tate characters is made.

sources.match: The rational proposition is deduced from finite crystalline subquotients; the plan makes its lattice and inverse-limit passage explicit.

nodes.title: Low-degree cohomology is zero or Tate
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper Q-scheme X with everywhere Witt good reduction, H^1_et(X_Q̄,Q_7)=0 and H^3_et(X_Q̄,Q_7)=0, and H^2_et(X_Q̄,Q_7)≅Q_7(−1)^b as G_Q-representations, where b=dim_Q7 H^2_et. The isomorphism need not choose a canonical basis.
hypotheses: The purity input is valid for proper smooth schemes without projectivity.
proofSteps: Apply the rational filtration to V_m=(H^m_et)^∨ for m=1,2,3.

Choose q outside 7N from the spread-out smooth proper model and compare eigenvalue absolute values: the pure dual cohomology has weight −m, while a nonzero grade χ^i has weight −2i. Exact characteristic-polynomial multiplicativity forces m=2i for each nonzero grade.
Odd m leave no grades and hence no cohomology. For m=2 the only grade is i=1, so V_1=V, V_2=0 and the whole action is χ, not merely its semisimplification. Dualize.
acceptance: Purity alone does not give semisimplicity. The special exhaustive filtration proves the full scalar action here.

sources.match: The purity argument eliminates the off-parity cyclotomic constituents and identifies degree two itself.

nodes.title: Fontaine’s low-degree Hodge vanishing
nodes.statement: For X/Q smooth proper with everywhere Witt good reduction, and natural i,j with i≠j and i+j≤3, the Q-vector space H^j(X,Ω_X^i) is zero. Equivalently h^{i,j}(X)=dim_Q H^j(X,Ω_X^i)=0. This includes total degree 0 vacuously and imposes no geometrical connectedness condition.
hypotheses: The degree inequality is ≤3. The off-diagonal condition is essential.
proofSteps: For m=i+j equal to 1 or 3 use the zero étale group. For m=2 use the Q_7(−1)-description: (C_7(i)⊗Q_7(−1))^G is zero unless i=1.
Use the Hodge–Tate comparison and faithful scalar extension Q→Q_7 to conclude the coherent Q-space is zero.
Total degree 0 has no pair with i≠j. This proof uses no Hodge symmetry or projectivity.
acceptance: h^{1,1} can be nonzero.
There is no assertion about h^{3,1} or h^{4,0}, both of total degree four.

sources.locator: Theorem 1 and Remark (a), p. 3; §2.1 and footnote, pp. 4–5
sources.match: This is the routed endpoint, with the full local-model generality and the correct total-degree restriction.

nodes.title: The global integral-model specialization
nodes.statement: If 𝓧 is a proper smooth scheme over Z and X=𝓧_Q, then H^j(X,Ω_X^i)=0 for i≠j and i+j≤3. More generally independent proper smooth Z_p-scheme models for every p suffice, without constructing a global Z-model.
proofSteps: Base change each model to W(F̄_p).
Apply the vanishing theorem; do not assert a reverse globalization of local models.
acceptance: Smooth projective spaces over Z meet all hypotheses.

sources.match: The original global theorem and the intermediate Z_p hypothesis are corollaries of the precise local endpoint.

nodes.title: The K3 Hodge obstruction has dimension one
nodes.statement: For a Q-scheme X whose base change to Q̄ is a K3 surface in K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness:K3.0/k3-surface, dim_Q H^0(X,Ω_X^2)=1. Use its smooth proper surface structure and geometric canonical trivialization, without requiring that the trivialization itself descend to Q.
hypotheses: The shared K3 predicate is smooth projective geometrically integral of dimension two, with trivial canonical sheaf and H^1(O)=0 over Q̄.
proofSteps: Over Q̄ identify Ω² with the canonical sheaf and then with O. Geometric integrality and properness give H^0(O)=Q̄.
Use coherent cohomology under field extension to descend the dimension, rather than a chosen global two-form.
acceptance: A projective abelian surface also has h^{2,0}=1 but fails the shared K3 H^1(O)=0 condition; it is not identified as K3.

sources.match: The application uses the nonzero K3 (2,0)-piece.

nodes.title: A K3 surface has a bad prime over the unramified Witt ring
nodes.statement: Let X/Q be smooth proper with geometric K3 base change in the shared predicate. There is a rational prime p for which X has no proper smooth scheme model over W(F̄_p). In particular X cannot have proper smooth scheme models over Z_p for all p, nor be the generic fibre of a proper smooth Z-scheme.
proofSteps: If all Witt models existed, LH.3 at (i,j)=(2,0) would force H^0(Ω²)=0.
This contradicts the K3 dimension-one theorem. Negate the universal model property.
acceptance: The repaired Enriques consumer supplies projective scheme models over Z_p, so meets the input.
Its projective generic K3 cover fits the shared definition; a smooth proper surface given only by intrinsic K3 conditions needs the K3 owner’s projectivity bridge.

sources.locator: Theorem 1 and Remark (a), p. 3; application motivated by Schröer Proposition 5.5
sources.match: The K3 obstruction is a direct consequence of the locally stated theorem, with no canonical-cover construction here.

nodes.title: Projective space tests the exact endpoint
nodes.statement: For P^n_Q and i,j≥0, H^j(P^n,Ω^i) is Q when i=j≤n and is zero otherwise. The standard P^n_Z-model verifies everywhere Witt good reduction, and for n≥1 its nonzero H^1(Ω^1) shows why the theorem retains the off-diagonal hypothesis. For n≥2 its H^2(Ω^2)=Q has total degree four, outside the low-degree conclusion.
proofSteps: Import the projective-space differential-cohomology computation from SF.2; its proof uses the Euler sequence, exterior powers and line-bundle cohomology.
Check the model by base change and compare each bidegree with the vanishing endpoint.
acceptance: This degree-four diagonal example does not show that an off-diagonal degree-four extension is false; no such stronger theorem is claimed.

sources.match: This is a worked model calculation of the conclusion and its limitations, not an additional Fontaine theorem.

Separately export spreading of a proper smooth Q-scheme X to a proper smooth Z[1/N]-scheme, and base change to its finite-field fibres at q∤N.
